items.title: "STANCE" and "TECHNIQUE" labels are too small/low contrast
items.what: In the bottom control region (e.g., third screenshot), the "STANCE" and "TECHNIQUE" text labels are small and low-contrast against the dark background, making it hard to distinguish which stick controls which input.
items.why: Players need clear visual cues to map touch inputs to game actions; unclear labels lead to confusion and missed inputs.
items.how: Increase font size of "STANCE" and "TECHNIQUE" labels by 20% and use a higher-contrast color (e.g., gold) to make them stand out against the dark control background.

items.title: "FIGHT" button number is too small
items.what: The "FIGHT" button (e.g., second screenshot) has a circular number (e.g., "2") that is too small and low-contrast, making it hard to see how many remaining fights are available.
items.why: Players need to know how many fights are left to plan their strategy; unclear numbers lead to uncertainty and frustration.
items.how: Increase the size of the circular number by 30% and use a bold, high-contrast color (e.g., white) to make it visible against the yellow button.

items.title: Techniques list icons are too small
items.what: In the "MOVES" menu (sixth screenshot), the circular icons next to each technique (e.g., Lunge Punch) are too small, making it hard to recognize the input pattern at a glance.
items.why: Players rely on visual icons to learn and recall moves; small icons slow down decision-making and increase cognitive load.
items.how: Increase the size of the technique icons by 25% and use a more distinct color (e.g., blue) to make them stand out against the dark menu background.

items.title: Settings checkboxes are too small
items.what: In the settings menu (seventh screenshot), the checkboxes for options like "Reduced motion" are too small, making them hard to tap accurately on touchscreens.
items.why: Small checkboxes lead to missed taps, frustration, and potential accidental setting changes.
items.how: Increase the size of all checkboxes by 40% and add a subtle border (e.g., gold) to make them more tappable and visible.

items.title: Fighters are too close to screen edges
items.what: In the gameplay screen (ninth screenshot), the fighters are positioned too close to the left and right edges of the screen, limiting visibility of their full body movements and attack animations.
items.why: Players need to see the full range of fighter animations to react and plan; edge proximity cuts off critical visual information.
items.how: Adjust the fighters' horizontal position to center them more in the screen, leaving at least 10% of the screen width on either side to display full animations.
